builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DWISE: Denoising Workload-Informed Scheduling Engine
summary: Replaces FCFS admission and prefill-priority scheduling (designed for autoregressive models) with remaining-work-based scheduling that shares rounds between prefill and denoising, using a lightweight admission-time predictor plus one refinement from first-round hidden states. Costs are modest: a predictor model at admission and scheduler complexity, but no additional model execution for the refinement. It can fail if workload prediction is inaccurate on out-of-distribution prompts, if the serving stack is not dLLM-based (the technique is irrelevant for AR-LLM serving), or if SGLang integration effort exceeds the small team's capacity.
rationale: The gain applies only when serving diffusion LLMs, which the reader likely does not do in production today, so adoption is premature but the scheduling insight is worth testing if dLLMs enter the stack.
technique: Workload-informed scheduling for diffusion LLM serving

claims.statement: Replaces FCFS admission and prefill-priority scheduling (designed for autoregressive models) with remaining-work-based scheduling that shares rounds between prefill and denoising, using a lightweight admission-time predictor plus one refinement from first-round hidden states. Costs are modest: a predictor model at admission and scheduler complexity, but no additional model execution for the refinement. It can fail if workload prediction is inaccurate on out-of-distribution prompts, if the serving stack is not dLLM-based (the technique is irrelevant for AR-LLM serving), or if SGLang integration effort exceeds the small team's capacity.
Reduces mean end-to-end latency over SGLang by 5.4x on average and up to 14.9x on five dLLMs under bursty workloads, while preserving task accuracy.
